name: Pascal's identity
whenToUse: Adding neighbouring binomial coefficients, building Pascal's triangle, or setting up a recursion by asking whether a particular item is chosen.
pitfall: The two coefficients you add must have the SAME top number and bottom numbers that differ by one; the result has top number one larger.
derivation: Fix one item. A $k$-subset of $n$ items either contains it ($\binom{n-1}{k-1}$ ways to pick the rest) or does not ($\binom{n-1}{k}$ ways).
